summary: Mason County, WA Forest Service lookout, also called Camp 3: in use by 1939, house moved off the hill in 1942 per Willhite Web; footings and an OSM ruin mark the summit.

facts.status_note: Lookout house moved to Dennie Ahl Hill in 1942 according to Willhite Web; old footings and an OpenStreetMap ruin mark the summit; no source dates these observations

access.note: Willhite Web's route follows Forest Service roads and says gates likely block the way; no source gives a public access rule

events.note: Lookout at Camp 3 in use by August 3, 1939 (newspaper articles, per Willhite Web); a Shelton-Mason County Journal item placed in the same 1939 passage names Johnnie Boyce as stationed there, but the quoted item gives no date
Lookout house moved to Dennie Ahl Hill per 1942 Aircraft Warning Service documents cited by Willhite Web
Newspaper item (quoted by Willhite Web) reports a fire near the old lookout at Camp 3, apparently started by pigeon hunters; the guide reads it as the lookout being gone by then

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register's description mentions a camp set up in 1946, while Willhite Web cites a newspaper item placing a lookout at Camp 3 by August 3, 1939. We record 1939 as the earliest evidence and treat the start date as unknown.

Willhite Web says the lookout house moved to Dennie Ahl Hill in 1942; firelookout.com's Dennie Ahl record gives a 1943 build and a 1971 destruction. The sources do not show that these are the same structure.
The 1946 item refers to the old lookout at Camp 3. Willhite Web reads this as proof the lookout was gone, which the newspaper itself does not state. The story reports it as the guide's reading.

notes_for_editor: The 1939 staffing and 1942 move rest on Willhite Web alone, quoting newspapers and 1942 AWS documents we could not check directly. The Boyce item's date is inferred from the sentence that precedes it on the page. The Dennie Ahl tower is a separate record and is cited only for its 1971 destruction; we did not establish that it is the house moved in 1942. Used one WebSearch and five page reads.
